response.markdown_report:
Prioritize a bounded catalog-ranking audit after the existing BERT4Rec integrity checks. At 20% progress, this offers an actionable next experiment without changing the trained model or assuming that training margins imply recommendation quality.

Three insights follow from the starting point. First, consumed-batch provenance can establish event alignment on captured examples. It cannot establish ranking quality beyond those examples. Second, Electronics’ reported negative-outranks-positive rate varies from 10.25% to 21.97% across supplied attempts. These training-exposed observations warrant investigation but do not identify a cause or validation winner. Third, predictor parity remains uncertified. Catalog diagnostics must therefore identify the exact scoring path they exercise.

Three insights follow from related work. BERT4Rec reconstructs masked items with bidirectional context [1]. Diagnostic next-item recovery should instead use strictly earlier context and an appended mask. Krichene and Rendle show that sampled evaluation can reverse model comparisons [2]. Comparing sampled and catalog ranks can expose candidate-set sensitivity, although the pinned host metric remains authoritative. The supplied popularity study reports accuracy tradeoffs across item-frequency groups [3]. Frequency-matched negatives provide a useful proposed stress test, without becoming an unbiased relevance measure.

These insights organize three directions: supervision integrity, candidate-set robustness, and deployment consistency. Their conceptual map is:

| Direction | Evidence unit | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|
| Existing provenance replay | Consumed event and loss | Catalog competition |
| Proposed rank audit | Fixed prefix and candidate universe | Held-out generalization |
| Predictor parity | Reloaded item-associated scores | User usefulness |

Three atomic ideas merit consideration. Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each out of ten; higher difficulty means more implementation effort.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Catalog versus sampled rank audit [1–3] | 4/7/3 | Directly tests candidate sensitivity; reusable; chunked scoring | Established components; no direct accuracy gain; catalog cost |
| Frequency-matched negative stress test [2,3] | 3/6/3 | Isolates an interpretable frequency control; simple reuse | Bin choices matter; relevance remains unknown; sparse bins |
| Exported-predictor score parity | 2/8/4 | Resolves a deployment uncertainty; broadly useful; no retraining | Engineering contribution; no usefulness guarantee; runner integration |

Select the first idea. Freeze one checkpoint per category; deterministically select at most 50 eligible training users/category and their last training target. Construct each prefix strictly before that event, retain earlier repeats, truncate to L−1, append MASK, left-pad, and read the final absolute position. Score eligible catalog items in chunks, excluding prefix-seen items except the target. Compare catalog rank with three reproducible draws of up to 99 unique uniform negatives from that same universe. Report sampled-hit/catalog-miss rates, rank variability, counts, and popularity/history strata.

Preserve all diagnostic interfaces and return unavailable reasons rather than healthy zeros. Preserve seeds, routing, training ceilings, trial-local artifacts and one model/category. Log diagnostic cost against the shared budget. Only unchanged host macro validation HR@10 selects revisions; these measurements describe training recovery, not generalization or immediate usefulness.

idea.description: Add a bounded, streaming catalog-ranking diagnostic to the corrected single-model BERT4Rec pipeline, comparing exact training-prefix catalog ranks with repeated sampled-candidate ranks from the same eligible universe.
idea.motivation: The supplied diagnostics establish uneven training-target separation but provide neither catalog-ranking evidence nor held-out gains. Candidate-set sensitivity is a concrete uncertainty that can be measured without modifying the backbone, training objective, or host evaluator.
idea.implementation_notes: This is an integration specification because the baseline source is absent. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), and every ModelView interface. Gate the audit on applicable structural checks; report unresolved provenance and exported-predictor parity separately. Use view.model as the actual network, with evaluation/inference mode and restoration of module modes and main-process RNG states in finally. Do not advance the production loader. Use dedicated diagnostic RNGs so candidate draws cannot perturb training. Predeclare a maximum of 50 eligible users per category, selected with seed 42; choose one last training target per user with at least one earlier event. Use only supplied training histories and catalog mappings. Retain legitimate earlier occurrences of the target. Define eligibility as catalog IDs excluding padding, MASK, and prefix-seen IDs, with the target explicitly retained. State that this diagnostic policy differs from full-history unseen-item recommendation and does not alter that native simulator path. Score each prefix once through appended-mask BERT4Rec inference and stream candidate scores in chunks using the same learned scorer. Rank deterministically by descending score then ascending catalog ID; use that tie rule for sampled ranks too. Count all eligible catalog items preceding the target without retaining all scores. Uniformly sample without replacement up to 99 eligible negatives using diagnostic seeds 42, 43, and 44; include the target once. Report actual candidate counts when the universe is small. Define sampled-hit/catalog-miss as sampled rank <=10 and catalog rank >10, with an explicit valid-user denominator. Return catalog HR@10, sampled HR@10, paired differences, hit flips, and rank summaries as training-exposed diagnostics only. Stratify using training-item frequencies and retained-prefix lengths, logging cutpoints and counts. Bootstrap users within category with all candidate draws grouped together; report each draw separately and equal-category macro summaries only when all four categories have observations. Bound execution and record elapsed diagnostic time; do not fabricate completed summaries after interruption. Keep DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, single-GPU execution, maximum 200 epochs, and 200 batches per completed epoch. Retain all four routes and exactly one independently trained checkpoint per category. No architecture, score fusion, checkpoint averaging, or additional fitted scorer is introduced. Preserve the embedded predictor writer and checkpoint configuration; any later inference change must update both. Host validation remains the sole selection criterion, and no test files or other trials are accessed.
idea.pseudocode:
class DiagnosisProbe:
    def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
        state = save_module_modes_and_main_process_rng()
        try:
            self.view.model.eval()
            with inference_mode():
                result = existing_family_safe_diagnostics_without_advancing_production_loader()
                if required_structural_checks_failed(result):
                    return add_unavailable_catalog_audit(result, reason='structural failure')
                users = seeded_select_eligible_training_users(limit=50, seed=42)
                for user in users:
                    history = supplied_training_history(user)
                    target = history[-1]
                    prefix = history[:-1][-(L - 1):]
                    tokens = left_pad(prefix + [MASK], L)
                    features = view.log2feats(tokens)[:, -1]
                    eligible = catalog_ids_excluding_prefix_seen_except_target(prefix, target)
                    target_score = view.predict_score(features, [target])
                    catalog_rank = 1
                    for chunk in chunks(eligible_without_target(eligible), configured_chunk_size):
                        scores = view.predict_score(features, chunk)
                        catalog_rank += count_preceding_target(scores, chunk, target_score, target,
                                                              tie_rule='ascending_item_id')
                    for draw_seed in [42, 43, 44]:
                        negatives = uniform_unique_sample(eligible - {target},
                                                          count=min(99, len(eligible) - 1),
                                                          dedicated_rng=draw_rng(draw_seed))
                        sampled_rank = score_target_rank_with_same_tie_rule(features, target, negatives)
                        record_training_recovery(user, catalog_rank, sampled_rank,
                                                 candidate_count=1 + len(negatives), draw_seed=draw_seed)
                aggregate_counts_strata_and_paired_user_bootstrap(result)
                return {'metrics': result.metrics, 'metric_definitions': result.definitions}
        finally:
            restore_module_modes_and_main_process_rng(state)

def diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    return interpretation_prompt(raw_diagnosis,
        require=['measured metrics', 'definitions', 'counts', 'candidate policy',
                 'exposure labels', 'unavailable reasons', 'diagnostic cost'],
        distinguish=['training recovery', 'predictor parity', 'host validation'],
        prohibit=['invented gains', 'causal preference claims', 'ensemble proposals'])

originality.positive: Combines event-aligned BERT4Rec recovery, streaming catalog ranks, and repeated candidate draws within the existing diagnostic contract.
originality.negative: Exact ranking and candidate-resampling audits are established techniques; the contribution is their controlled integration.

future_potential.positive: Can distinguish candidate sensitivity from weak catalog competition and inform subsequent single-model loss or sampling experiments.
future_potential.negative: Training recovery remains exposure-confounded, and the audit itself neither improves validation accuracy nor establishes actionable usefulness.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses the existing encoder and scorer, requires no retraining, and supports bounded chunked computation.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct eligibility, repeated-target handling, stable ties, uncertainty accounting, and large-catalog runtime require careful integration.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Provides the family-specific basis for appended-mask next-item scoring.
limitations: Interior masked-item recovery and terminal prediction use different available context.
Its objective alone does not certify this implementation's integrity or ranking quality.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can yield inconsistent model comparisons.
Motivates measuring candidate-set sensitivity alongside catalog ranks.
limitations: Does not establish that the supplied BERT4Rec checkpoints exhibit a particular ranking failure.
Does not justify replacing the task's pinned sampled validation protocol.

related_work.title: Sequential recommendation negative-sampling study supplied in the search results
contributions: The supplied summary reports head, middle, and tail accuracy differences under alternative negative-sampling policies.
Motivates training-frequency stratification and a frequency-matched diagnostic control.
limitations: Reported tradeoffs do not establish a popularity shortcut in these checkpoints.
Frequency matching is a proposed stress test rather than an unbiased estimator of relevance.
